how.title: How to apply in the shareholder quota

steps.title: Buy one parent share
steps.body: Buy before 3:30 PM IST on the trading day before the RHP date. One share of the listed parent is usually enough; the RHP sets the exact rule.

steps.title: It lands in your demat
steps.body: Trades settle the next trading day, so a share bought on the RHP date itself arrives too late.

steps.title: Eligibility is fixed
steps.body: Everyone holding the parent in demat on this date can bid in the quota. It is often about a week before the IPO opens.

steps.title: Bid in both categories
steps.body: Bid up to ₹2 lakh as a shareholder, and apply as retail or HNI too. The two are not counted as multiple bids.

steps.title: Allotted from a separate pool
steps.body: The quota, up to 10% of the issue, is allotted only among eligible shareholders. That pool is apart from retail, not instead of it.

items.q: What is a shareholder quota in an IPO?
items.a: When a listed company takes a subsidiary or group company public, the IPO can set aside up to 10% of the issue for the listed parent's shareholders. Only people who hold the parent's shares on the eligibility date can bid in that portion.

items.q: When do I need to own the parent's shares?
items.a: On the date of the red herring prospectus (RHP), or the record date the RHP names. The shares must be in your demat account by then, so a purchase on that day may be too late.

items.q: What is the last day to buy the parent share?
items.a: The trading day before the RHP date, by 3:30 PM IST. Trades in India settle the next trading day (T+1), so a share bought on the RHP date reaches your demat too late. Each IPO under Buy before shows this day and a countdown.

items.q: Can I apply in both the shareholder and retail categories?
items.a: Yes. You can bid up to ₹2 lakh in the shareholder category and also apply as retail or HNI from the same PAN. The two are not counted as multiple bids, so you have a chance in each pool.

items.q: How do I apply in the shareholder quota?
items.a: Apply through your broker or bank as usual and pick the shareholder category as the investor type. Use the demat account that held the parent share on the RHP date, and bid up to ₹2 lakh at cut-off.

items.q: Can the shareholder quota be dropped?
items.a: Yes. A draft offer document (DRHP) can change before the final RHP, and a company that only announced an IPO has not committed to anything yet. That is why each IPO here shows its stage and a link to its offer document.

We check offer documents filed with SEBI, NSE and BSE every day for a shareholder reservation and the parent it names. We also read BSE announcements from listed companies whose board has approved taking a subsidiary public; our team reviews each one before it shows here as rumoured. Once an IPO lists it moves to Recently listed for six months. A SEBI approval that lapses without dates moves back to Rumoured, marked lapsed, for a year. A rumour with no draft after a year drops off.

disclaimer: This list is gathered from offer documents, exchange filings and exchange announcements.
